answer: Scarce sync-window allocation.** Each identity is assigned a narrow, verifiable timing slot derived from its persistent state history; a dune of accumulated clock drift must accrue before a new identity is admitted. The rule: registration requires proof of sustained low-latency participation across many prior cycles, so mass-created identities cannot all fit the dawn admission batch. Attackers pay measurable cost by maintaining thousands of parallel nodes through the full tide of observation before any one identity matures.
